messages:
devon: Noticed failing key-rotation job on a customer's private cluster. Audit shows rotation started but no KMS decrypts for new key. Logs: 'rotation: unable to fetch key: forbidden' and agent reports 'watcher: secret mount read-only'. Anyone seen secret/token perms cause this?

anya: That 'forbidden' usually means SA lost permission to get/list secrets or the mutating webhook couldn't update the secret. Did they apply the new RBAC policy for `rotation-runner` yesterday?

frank: I saw a diff in their PR: removed `secrets/get` on namespace infra to tighten RBAC, replaced with `secrets/list` only. That will break `kubectl exec` style rotation that reads by name.

devon: Customer says they tightened network policies at the same time to deny pod-to-pod within infra ns. Could block the agent sidecar that performs KMS calls.

kate: Quick checklist: 1) confirm serviceaccount bound to rolebinding that includes `secrets/get` 2) verify netpol allows egress to KMS endpoint 3) check pod security context for `fsGroup` changes affecting secret mounts.

devon: They ran `kubectl auth can-i get secrets --as=system:serviceaccount:infra:rotation-runner -n infra` and got 'no'. So RBAC is the immediate culprit.

frank: But why did audit show rotation started? The job created a temp keyobject but couldn't complete final decrypt/verify step. So audit entries are partial. This matters for compliance evidence.

anya: For mitigation propose minimal change: add back `secrets/get` scoped to the single secret name via a Role with resourceNames. Example:```yaml
kind: Role
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
metadata:
  name: rotation-read-only
  namespace: infra
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["secrets"]
  resourceNames: ["rotation-key-secret"]
  verbs: ["get"]
```

anya: That keeps RBAC tight but restores rotation.

devon: Also flagged: audit logs have no `userAgent` for the rotation job because agent buffers were dropped during a node reboot. We should ask for `kubectl get events -n infra --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp -o wide` to correlate.

ops-bot: Deploy job rotation-runner v3.2.7 -> v3.2.8 scheduled to canary nodes. Monitor audit events for 'rotation_complete' and KMS decrypt counts for 10m.

audit-bot: Created ticket APT-2026-198: 'priv-deploy rotation audit gap'. Linked to INC-2026-17.

frank: One oddity: the customer's KMS integration uses mutual TLS with certs rotated by the rotation job. If the job fails mid-rotation, old certs still valid but new key not present in KMS, causing decrypt errors for recent tokens. We should add an atomic swap pattern in our rotation playbook.

anya: Agreed. For now mitigation steps to give to customer: 1) Apply the Role with resourceNames for rotation secret 2) Temporarily relax intra-namespace netpol to allow pod-to-pod between rotation-runner and agent sidecar (we can provide a minimal netpol snippet) 3) Restart rotation-job pod after RBAC change 4) Provide `kubectl logs` for rotation-runner and agent for the failed run.

devon: Netpol snippet (minimal):```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-rotation-sidecar
  namespace: infra
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: rotation-runner
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  - Ingress
  ingress:
  - from:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: agent-sidecar
```

kate: Addendum: we should avoid cluster-wide hostNetwork or broad egress opens. Recommend scoping to namespace and serviceaccount. Also ask them to capture `kubectl describe rolebinding rotation-binding -n infra` to ensure binding targets correct SA.

devon: Customer applied Role and restarted. They report rotation completed and audit shows 'rotation_complete' entries. I'll close the incident when they confirm audit retention has the full trace.

frank: Postmortem items for us: 1) update rotation playbook to include RBAC preflight check 2) add an atomic-swap example to our docs 3) include netpol troubleshooting steps in private-deploy runbook.

anya: I'll file follow-ups and draft the doc changes. devon, please paste the customer's `kubectl logs` here once you have them for our records.

devon: Will do. Thanks all :v:
